subject: Supply Chain & Logistics
title: The Panama Canal
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Panama Canal usable.

hook.text: Building the Panama Canal killed over 25,000 workers. It still became the most important shortcut on Earth.

buildup.text: Opened in 1914, it connects the Atlantic and Pacific without the 8,000-mile trip around South America.

discovery.text: Ships are lifted 85 feet through locks, cross a lake, and descend on the other side. An engineering marvel.

twist.text: The canal is too narrow for the largest modern ships. A $5.25 billion expansion opened in 2016.

climax.text: In 2023, drought reduced canal traffic by 40%. Climate change now threatens this vital trade route.

punchline.text: Even the greatest shortcuts have limits.

quiz.question: What recent threat reduced Panama Canal traffic?
